adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10045: insured's warehouse (Flood Zone 2) suffered flood damage on 15 June 2024 when water entered from a nearby river during heavy rainfall. No prior flood event at this location this policy year. Claimed amount GBP 180,000.
why: A single good search on the flood sub-limit/deductible clauses (Endorsement 1, clauses 2-3) should both decide and ground this claim.

adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10046: insured's distribution centre flooded again on 20 July 2024, six weeks (42 days) after an earlier flood at the same site on 8 June 2024. No record of the flood barriers, non-return valves or sump pumps having been tested in the 60 days before the second event.
why: The denial is correct only if it is grounded in clause 4.3 (Exclusion Code E-17, the sequential-event exclusion) or 4.4 (its carve-out). A generic first search surfaces the flood sub-limit/deductible clauses (1-3) and clause 4.1, which look plausible but do not govern a *second* flood event -- deciding this correctly needs a second, more targeted search for the exclusion code itself.

adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10047: a ransomware attack on 3 September 2024 triggered a fire in the server room that caused physical damage to computer hardware and the surrounding building fabric. No ransom was paid and no data was lost; the insured seeks cover for the physical fire damage only.
why: The broad cyber exclusion (Section 2) reads like a clean denial until Section 3's write-back is found: physical fire/explosion damage resulting from a Cyber Incident is carved back in. Grounding must cite the write-back, not just the exclusion.

adjuster_notes: Claim ref ABC/2024/778: business interruption following a burst water main that caused a production outage lasting 5 days from 2 November 2024. The outage was notified to the risk manager on 25 November 2024.
why: The claim reference is not in CLM-YYYY-NNNNN form. The path question here is not which clause got cited -- it's whether check_assertions actually surfaces the real defect (claim_number_format=FAIL) rather than the agent silently finalizing over it.

adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10048: insured is claiming for a company vehicle stolen from the staff car park on 10 August 2024. Claimed amount GBP 32,000.
why: Motor theft is outside this endorsement pack entirely. The honest path here is a search that comes up empty -- no citation -- not a confident citation of an unrelated clause.
